greeting.desconocido.1: A stranger? I haven't seen you around %2$s.
greeting.desconocido.2: Good day. Have you come far?
greeting.desconocido.3: Hello, traveller. We are quiet folk here.
greeting.desconocido.4: Hm. And who might you be?
greeting.desconocido.5: If you've come to trade, fine. If not, fine too, but don't touch anything.
greeting.desconocido.6: Not many folk pass through %2$s. Are you lost?
greeting.desconocido.7: Good day... or whatever it is. I don't often talk to strangers.
greeting.desconocido.8: Fair warning: the golem doesn't trust anyone who arrives in a hurry.

greeting.conocido.2: Your face rings a bell. You helped with something on the board, didn't you?
greeting.conocido.3: Good day, %1$s. What brings you to %2$s?
greeting.conocido.5: I thought I knew those boots.
greeting.conocido.6: %1$s! I'd started to think you weren't coming back.
greeting.conocido.7: Hello. Didn't get lost this time, eh?
greeting.conocido.8: Look, it's our errand-runner. How goes it, %1$s?

greeting.amigo.1: %1$s, my friend! Sit down a moment.
greeting.amigo.2: So glad to see you. They speak well of you in %2$s.
greeting.amigo.3: Look who's back! Come in, come in.
greeting.amigo.4: %1$s! We were just talking about you. Good things, don't worry.
greeting.amigo.5: Come here, I've fresh bread and nobody to share it with.
greeting.amigo.6: It's been too long, %1$s. %2$s missed you.
greeting.amigo.7: There you are! The children kept asking after you.
greeting.amigo.8: My friend, how's the world treating you?

greeting.heroe.1: The hero of %2$s! The children won't stop talking about you.
greeting.heroe.2: %1$s, it's an honour. Whatever you need.
greeting.heroe.4: %1$s, in the flesh! Hold on, let me dust myself off.
greeting.heroe.5: All of %2$s owes you something. Me most of all.
greeting.heroe.6: My grandmother says she'll keep you in her prayers. And in her will.
greeting.heroe.7: %1$s is back! Somebody ring the bell.
greeting.heroe.8: With you here, even the golem stands up straighter.

reputation.desconocido.1: We're a bit wary of strangers here. Nothing personal.
reputation.desconocido.2: If you want to be known, look at the board on the square.
reputation.desconocido.3: Don't take it badly, but I can't tell yet if you're to be trusted.
reputation.desconocido.4: Words blow away on the wind. In %2$s we watch what folk do.

reputation.conocido.1: The bailiff says you keep your word. That counts for a lot here.
reputation.conocido.2: They don't look at you funny at the market any more, have you noticed?
reputation.conocido.3: Some folk greet you by name now. That's a good sign.
reputation.conocido.4: Keep this up and %2$s will count you as one of our own.

reputation.amigo.1: I keep the best of the week for you, just so you know.
reputation.amigo.2: You have a home in %2$s whenever you want.
reputation.amigo.3: If you ever need a hand, there are plenty of them here.
reputation.amigo.4: I don't bolt the door any more when I see you coming, %1$s.

reputation.heroe.1: Someday someone will write a song about you. I hope it rhymes.
reputation.heroe.2: As long as you're around, we sleep soundly.
reputation.heroe.3: They tell your name round the fire now, %1$s.
reputation.heroe.4: If %2$s had statues, yours would be the first.

family.llanuras.1: From here you can see anyone coming a league away.
family.llanuras.2: The plains wind carries off your worries and your hat.
family.llanuras.3: Out here the wheat runs as far as the eye can see.
family.llanuras.4: Plains horses won't let you ride them the first time.
family.llanuras.5: There's nowhere to hide on the plains. Not from rain, not from gossip.
family.llanuras.6: The poppies come up on their own along the field edges. Nobody plants them.

family.bosque.1: There are mushrooms in the forest that heal and some that don't. Learn which are which.
family.bosque.2: The birches sing when the wind blows. Listen.
family.bosque.3: Firewood's never short here, but you ask the forest first.
family.bosque.4: If you hear a wolf, don't run. They run faster.
family.bosque.5: The oldest oaks were here long before the village.
family.bosque.6: In autumn the forest floor crunches like toasted bread.

family.oscuro.1: Under these oaks it is never quite daytime.
family.oscuro.2: Don't stray from the lanterns after nightfall. Trust me.
family.oscuro.3: The giant mushrooms grow where the light can't reach. So do other things.
family.oscuro.4: Here the trees touch overhead. The sky is just a rumour.
family.oscuro.5: My grandfather said the dark forest has a memory. And a grudge.
family.oscuro.6: Never whistle among the black oaks. Something might whistle back.

family.taiga.1: The spruces smell of resin and of winter coming.
family.taiga.2: Around here the foxes even steal the eggs from the henhouse.
family.taiga.3: Sweet berries prick your fingers, but the jam is worth it.
family.taiga.4: In the taiga winter doesn't knock: one day it's simply there.
family.taiga.5: The old ones carved runes in the trunks so they wouldn't lose their way.
family.taiga.6: A good axe, a good fire, a good coat. Anything more is extra.

family.nieve.1: Here you learn quickly never to let the fire go out.
family.nieve.2: The snow covers everything, even the wolves' tracks.
family.nieve.3: Don't trust the lake ice. It creaks before it breaks, but not long before.
family.nieve.4: Polar bears are calm. Until they aren't.
family.nieve.5: In %2$s we count winters, not years.
family.nieve.6: Watch out for powder snow: some sank in and never came out.

family.desierto.1: Water is worth more than gold here. Well, almost.
family.desierto.2: By day it scorches and by night it freezes. The desert knows no middle ground.
family.desierto.3: My grandfather planted palms along the water channel. They still give shade.
family.desierto.4: The sand keeps secrets better than any chest.
family.desierto.5: When the day cools, the courtyard with the fountain is the best place in the world.
family.desierto.6: The cactus asks for nothing and endures everything. Learn from it.

family.sabana.1: The acacias give little shade, but they give it to everyone alike.
family.sabana.2: The wild horses come down to drink at sunset.
family.sabana.3: Dry grass here catches fire from nothing. Careful with torches.
family.sabana.4: The plateau llamas spit, but they'll carry whatever you load on them.
family.sabana.5: At midday the savanna horizon shimmers with heat.
family.sabana.6: When the rain finally comes, we all go out to get soaked.

family.jungla.1: In the jungle everything grows, especially what you don't want.
family.jungla.2: The parrots repeat what we say. Mind your words.
family.jungla.3: You won't find better cocoa than ours anywhere around.
family.jungla.4: If an ocelot stares at you, keep still. It's only making up its mind.
family.jungla.5: The vines close the path in a week. You always have to cut it open again.
family.jungla.6: They say the jungle eats temples. Slowly, but it eats them.

family.pantano.1: The swamp mist hides more than it seems.
family.pantano.2: The frogs sing all night. You get used to it. More or less.
family.pantano.3: If you see a hut with cauldrons steaming, don't knock.
family.pantano.4: The mud here cures corns. So says the old woman at the mill.
family.pantano.5: Slimes come out at full moon. Don't ask me why.
family.pantano.6: Never drink anything offered by a woman in a pointed hat.

family.cerezos.1: When the petals fall it looks like pink snow.
family.cerezos.2: The cherry-blossom bees make the sweetest honey around.
family.cerezos.3: Under the cherry trees we speak softly. It's the custom.
family.cerezos.4: Every spring someone proposes beneath the great cherry tree.
family.cerezos.5: I sweep the petals every morning. Every evening they're back.
family.cerezos.6: In %2$s we say the blossom lasts so little so that you'll look at it properly.

family.badlands.1: This red earth holds gold, if you know where to look.
family.badlands.2: The abandoned mines creak at night. I wouldn't go near them.
family.badlands.3: The sun bakes the coloured clay here. It looks painted by hand.
family.badlands.4: More than one came looking for a fortune and stayed to raise goats.
family.badlands.5: The red dust gets into everything: your clothes, your food, your dreams.
family.badlands.6: Round here, whoever finds a vein doesn't tell even their own mother.

family.costa.1: The sea brings everything: fish, driftwood and the odd bottle.
family.costa.2: When the lighthouse goes dark, we know a storm is coming.
family.costa.3: Everything tastes of salt here, even the bread.
family.costa.4: The turtles come back to the same beach every year. Like the sailors.
family.costa.5: Never turn your back on the sea. It never turns its back on you.
family.costa.6: My father said you can hear the drowned in seashells.

time.morning.1: Getting up early in %2$s is easy: the rooster shows no mercy.
time.morning.2: A good day to start something new, don't you think?
time.morning.3: My eyes are still half shut. Talk slowly.
time.morning.4: The morning dew is the best part of the day. After that it all gets complicated.
time.morning.5: Up already, %1$s? Either you slept very little or very well.

time.afternoon.1: At this hour only the cats nap in peace.
time.afternoon.2: Half the work is already done. The other half, tomorrow.
time.afternoon.3: A full belly makes for slow thinking. Everyone says so.
time.afternoon.4: Mid-afternoon the square empties. A good time for a chat.
time.afternoon.5: There's still light for a good stretch of work.

time.evening.1: The sun is setting. We'll have to shut ourselves in soon.
time.evening.2: At this hour the sky over %2$s turns every colour.
time.evening.3: Every house smells of supper already.
time.evening.4: Bring in whatever you've left outside, %1$s. Night won't be long.
time.evening.5: This is the hour the bats leave the caves.

time.night.1: What are you doing up at this hour? There are zombies out there.
time.night.2: At night you hear strange things beyond the wall.
time.night.3: Keep your voice down, the neighbours are asleep.
time.night.4: You see the stars better from here than from anywhere.
time.night.5: If you hear bones rattling out there, it isn't the wind.

weather.clear.1: What a clear day. You can see all the way to the horizon.
weather.clear.2: In this sun, washing dries in no time.
weather.clear.3: Not a cloud. Even the golem looks pleased.
weather.clear.4: A sky like this makes you want to set off on a journey.
weather.clear.5: Good weather for working the fields. And for not working them.

weather.rain.1: This rain is good for the fields but bad for my knees.
weather.rain.2: If it keeps raining like this, the river will burst its banks.
weather.rain.3: Come in out of that, you'll be soaked to the bone.
weather.rain.4: My roof leaks right over the bed. Every time.
weather.rain.5: Fish bite better in the rain. So the fishermen say.

weather.snow.1: More snow. We'll have to clear the roof again.
weather.snow.2: In this cold even the skeletons shiver.
weather.snow.3: The children are already building snowmen in the square.
weather.snow.4: Wrap up, %1$s. Snow is deceiving: it looks soft and it bites.
weather.snow.5: When it snows like this, the whole world goes quiet.

weather.thunder.1: That lightning struck close! Keep away from the trees.
weather.thunder.2: In a storm not even creepers come out. Well, they do.
weather.thunder.3: They say lightning once turned a pig into something horrible. I believe it.
weather.thunder.4: Every thunderclap makes me jump. Don't laugh.
weather.thunder.5: In a storm like this, better not leave %2$s. Believe me.

general.1: Life in %2$s is simple, and I like it that way.
general.2: The iron golem has looked at me oddly since I painted a flower on it.
general.3: The well on the square gives the freshest water around.
general.4: They say the mayor snores so loud he scares the bats.
general.5: Take care, %1$s. The world is big and not always kind.
general.6: My bed is the only thing that's truly mine. And I defend it.
general.7: Every bell here has its own voice. The one on the square is the grumpiest.
general.8: I can't read, but I can count emeralds. That's enough for me.
general.9: The cats of %2$s rule more than the mayor does.
general.10: If you see someone in a green robe with a sour face, that's my cousin.
general.11: I've lived in %2$s all my life and I still get lost in the market.
general.12: A good neighbour is worth more than a full chest.
general.13: When I was young I wanted to see the world. Then I saw a zombie and got over it.
general.14: Hens lay more if you sing to them. Don't look at me like that.
general.15: In %2$s everyone knows everyone. For better and for worse.
general.16: Work goes better with a song. Pity I don't know any.
general.17: I keep one emerald put by for a bad day. It hasn't come yet.
general.18: What patience can't mend, bread usually can.
general.19: You're not from here, that's plain. You smell of the road.
general.20: What you hear most here is bells, hens and gossip.

rumor.1: They say a merchant came through last night with three llamas and no hurry at all.
rumor.2: The smith's daughter is engaged. Or so she says.
rumor.3: Someone has seen strange lights in the hills. I'm sure it's nothing.
rumor.4: In the next village they bake horrible bread. Don't tell them I said so.
rumor.5: We haven't seen the wandering trader for days. I hope he's well.
rumor.6: The shepherd swears one of his sheep came back dyed pink. He says it wasn't him.
rumor.7: Someone leaves flowers on the librarian's door at night. Nobody knows who.
rumor.8: A woodcutter heard bells deep in the forest, where there are no bells at all.
rumor.9: The children say they saw a skeleton riding a spider. I don't believe them. Not entirely.
rumor.10: A traveller turned up yesterday with scorched clothes and wouldn't say where from.
rumor.11: The cleric buys more candles than anyone could need. What does he want with so many?
rumor.12: They say someone pulled a trident out of the sea. And the sea wanted it back.
rumor.13: The last caravan had a man who spoke to no one. He left in the night.
rumor.14: A fisherman swears he saw a city under the water. Mind you, he drinks.
rumor.15: Bandits have been seen on the roads again. If you travel, don't go alone.
rumor.16: The old woman in the last house says she talks to the cats. And that they answer.
rumor.17: For weeks now the golem has stood staring at the forest. It must have seen something.
rumor.18: Someone found a compass that doesn't point north. Sold it straight away, of course.
rumor.19: They say there are caves in the mountains where you can hear the stone breathing.
rumor.20: A cartographer came through with a half-finished map. Said there were things he didn't dare draw.

busy.1: Not now, I have work to do. If you want to trade, go ahead.
busy.2: We'll talk later, my stew is burning.
busy.3: Give me a while, you've caught me busy.
busy.4: Shh, I'm resting. Come back later.
busy.5: Not right now, %1$s. My head's somewhere else.
busy.6: Leave me be, I've been on my feet all day.

farewell.2: Come back whenever you like. We'll be here.
farewell.4: Until next time. And don't forget %2$s.
farewell.5: Keep your eyes open, night comes without warning.
farewell.6: If you see my cousin out there, tell him he owes me an emerald.
farewell.7: Safe travels. And eat something, you're all skin and bones.
farewell.8: May the road go easy on you, %1$s.

hint.unique.1: I'll tell you something nobody knows: when I was young I saw ‘%1$s’, to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. I never went back.
hint.unique.2: My father used to tell me about ‘%1$s’. It lies to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. They say something guards it.
hint.unique.3: If you want real adventure: ‘%1$s’, to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. I turned back at the gate.
hint.unique.4: Once I slept out in the open in the shadow of ‘%1$s’. To the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. Didn't sleep a wink.
hint.unique.5: To the %2$s, about %3$s blocks off, stands ‘%1$s’. From afar it looks peaceful. Up close, it doesn't.
hint.unique.6: The biggest thing I ever saw: ‘%1$s’. Walk %3$s blocks or so to the %2$s and you'll see it before you get there.

hint.medium.1: When I travelled I stopped at a place like that: ‘%1$s’, to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks from here.
hint.medium.2: To the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away, there's ‘%1$s’. Ask for me if anyone is still there.
hint.medium.3: Don't tell anyone: ‘%1$s’, to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks. Worth the walk.
hint.medium.4: I sheltered from the rain one night at ‘%1$s’. To the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. They treated me well. I think.
hint.medium.5: Head %2$s, about %3$s blocks. That's where ‘%1$s’ is. Bring food, the way feels long.
hint.medium.6: My last stop before coming home was ‘%1$s’, to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks off. I still remember the smell.

hint.mine.1: There's ‘%1$s’ to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. I went down once and heard picks in the dark.
hint.mine.2: If you're after ore, ‘%1$s’, to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. Take plenty of torches.
hint.mine.3: I worked a season at ‘%1$s’. To the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. I quit when my torch went out by itself.
hint.mine.4: To the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away, you go down into ‘%1$s’. The minecarts still roll. Nobody pushes them.
hint.mine.5: An old miner took me to ‘%1$s’, to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks. I came out with full pockets and shaking hands.
hint.mine.6: ‘%1$s’, to the %2$s, about %3$s blocks away. Down there the air tastes of iron. And of something else.

hint.withheld.1: I've seen the world, yes... but I don't tell just anyone. Earn the trust of %2$s.
hint.withheld.2: I know of a place, but I don't know you well enough yet, %1$s.
hint.withheld.3: Help out a bit on the board and maybe I'll tell you what I saw on my travels.
hint.withheld.4: The secrets of the road are earned, %1$s. It isn't your turn yet.
hint.withheld.5: Come back when they say your name in %2$s without frowning.
hint.withheld.6: I could tell you a great many things. But first I want to see what you're worth.

hint.told.1: I've already told what I know. The rest you'll have to find out yourself.
hint.told.2: My secret is already told. Maybe someone else in %2$s knows more.
hint.told.3: Have you been to see what I told you? Then I've nothing more to tell.
hint.told.4: What I knew is yours now, %1$s. Look after it.

hint.nothing.1: I travelled a lot, but around here I saw nothing worth telling.
hint.nothing.2: What I saw on my travels is too far from here.
hint.nothing.3: Round here there's only fields and more fields. Believe me, I walked every one.
hint.nothing.4: I'd like to help you, %1$s, but there's nothing near %2$s worth an adventure.
